document.title: Searching for the Taliban's Hidden Message (Islama 05749)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] A Taliban official, name excised and probably Deputy Foreign Minister Abdul Jalil, breaks from the usual Taliban responses and is far less obstreperous. Ambassador Milam says the U.S. is not out to destroy the Taliban but that the bin Laden issue is supremely important and must be resolved first. Excised.

persons.name: William B. Milam
persons.role: US Ambassador to Pakistan; met a Taliban interlocutor on 17 September 2000

mentions.quote: CLASSIFIED BY AMBASSADOR WILLIAM B. MILAM.
IN ORDER TO MEET AMBASSADOR SEPTEMBER 17.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Subject of US demands; sheltered in Afghanistan by the Taliban; accused of the embassy bombings

mentions.quote: DID NOT PRODUCE AN OFFER TO RELINQUISH USAMA BIN LADIN
HAD JUST BLOWN UP TWO EMBASSIES, KILLING MANY AMERICANS

persons.name: Mullah Omar
persons.role: Taliban supreme leader; issued the decree forbidding poppy cultivation and a new education edict

mentions.quote: TALIBAN SUPREME LEADER MULLAH OMAR'S DECREE FORBIDDING POPPY CULTIVATION
DEGREE TO WHICH WOULD BE SPEAKING FOR ALL THE TALIBAN, ESPECIALLY OMAR.

persons.name: Ahmad Shah Masood
persons.role: Northern Alliance military leader opposing the Taliban

mentions.quote: THE OPPOSITION CLAIMS TO SUPPORT PEACE, BUT MASOOD ROUTINELY BREAKS HIS WORD.

persons.role: US Under Secretary of State; previously delivered similar messages to the Taliban

events.description: Lengthy meeting between the US Ambassador and a Taliban interlocutor (name redacted) who came from Kandahar via Quetta; Bin Ladin was not relinquished, but the tone was notably different.
Embassy Islamabad sent a NODIS cable reporting the meeting to the State Department.
US cruise missile attack, referred to as a response to the embassy bombings and aimed at Bin Ladin.
Ambassador Milam held a lengthy, confidential meeting with a senior Taliban interlocutor on bin Ladin, sanctions, aid gestures, and the possibility of a US-Taliban relationship.
Embassy Islamabad transmitted the NODIS cable to State recommending small, low-cost gestures to the Taliban, including a favorable statement on the drug ban and advance notice of assistance.
US cruise missile strike on bin Ladin, explained as self-defense after the embassy bombings in Africa; the Taliban interlocutor referred to it.
Bin Ladin is described as having blown up two US embassies, killing many Americans and more Africans, shortly before the US cruise missile strike.

Ambassador Milam met a Taliban representative in Islamabad; the representative sought assurances US not seeking Taliban destruction and said Taliban would work behind the scenes; no offer to relinquish bin Ladin.
Taliban interlocutor traveled overland from Kandahar to Quetta, then flew to Islamabad as the UN flight did not operate.
Embassy Islamabad sent NODIS cable 5749 to Washington reporting the meeting.
US cruise missile attack, discussed as self-defense against bin Ladin after the embassy bombings.
Mullah Omar's decree forbidding poppy cultivation, followed by anti-narcotics teaching in madrassahs.
Phone call from Mujahid in New York reported in Ref A.
UNDCP announced a withdrawal from Afghanistan within the six-plus-two regional action plan.

relationships.detail: The US says UN sanctions stem from the Taliban policy of harboring Bin Ladin; the direction is Bin Ladin sheltered by the Taliban.
relationships.quote: RATHER DUE TO THEIR POLICY OF HARBORING BIN LADIN.

relationships.detail: The Ambassador met a Taliban interlocutor in Islamabad on 17 September 2000.
relationships.quote: IN ORDER TO MEET AMBASSADOR SEPTEMBER 17.

relationships.detail: Taliban interlocutor said the Taliban saved Bin Ladin's life and attempt to control him.
relationships.quote: IF WE HAVE SAVED HIS LIFE, PERHAPS WE HAVE SAVED AMERICAN LIVES, TOO. WE ATTEMPT TO CONTROL HIM.

relationships.detail: Omar is the Taliban supreme leader who issues decrees the Taliban enforce.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN SUPREME LEADER MULLAH OMAR'S DECREE FORBIDDING POPPY CULTIVATION

relationships.detail: Masood's Northern Alliance is the Taliban's military/political opponent.
relationships.quote: MARGINALIZING MASOOD'S NORTHERN ALLIANCE AS A MILITARY/POLITICAL FORCE

relationships.detail: Taliban and Northern Alliance at war and growing apart.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN AND THE NORTHERN ALLIANCE HAD MOVED FARTHER AND FARTHER APART

relationships.detail: The Ambassador met a Taliban interlocutor to discuss the bin Ladin issue and US-Taliban engagement.
relationships.quote: USG POLICY HAS ALWAYS BEEN TO TRY TO FIND A WAY TO ENGAGE THE TALIBAN

relationships.detail: The Ambassador held a lengthy confidential meeting with the Taliban interlocutor, whose name is redacted. Mujahid is the nearest candidate in the entity list, so the identification is inferred.
relationships.quote: AS THE (LENGTHY) MEETING

relationships.detail: The Ambassador heads the Embassy, which sent the cable (signed MILAM).
relationships.quote: MILAM

relationships.detail: The Embassy cable was sent to SECSTATE Washington, marked NODIS and IMMEDIATE.
relationships.quote: FM AMEMBASSY ISLAMABAD TO SECSTATE WASHDC IMMEDIATE

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin is harbored by the Taliban, which is the basis of the US sanctions against them. Direction is bin Ladin to Taliban as provider.
relationships.quote: HARBORING BIN LADIN. IF BIN LADIN IS EXPELLED TO A PLACE WHERE HE CAN BE BROUGHT TO JUSTICE

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin's existence in Afghanistan under Taliban protection is the major US issue with the Taliban.
relationships.quote: UBL IS OUR MAJOR PROBLEM WITH THE TALIBAN

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin's presence in Afghanistan is described as a major US issue.
relationships.quote: HIS EXISTENCE IN AFGHANISTAN (OR ANYWHERE ELSE) IS A MAJOR ISSUE FOR THE U.S.

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin is described as the sworn enemy of the United States, which acts against him in self-defense.
relationships.quote: A MAN WHO PROCLAIMS HIMSELF THE SWORN ENEMY OF THE UNITED STATES AND ITS PEOPLE

relationships.detail: The Taliban appear to be winning and can look forward to marginalizing Masood's Northern Alliance.
relationships.quote: MARGINALIZING MASOOD'S NORTHERN ALLIANCE AS A MILITARY/POLITICAL FORCE

relationships.detail: The Northern Alliance is referred to as Masood's.
relationships.quote: MASOOD'S NORTHERN ALLIANCE

relationships.detail: Omar is the Taliban leader. The Taliban interlocutor may not speak for all the Taliban, especially Omar.
relationships.quote: SPEAKING FOR ALL THE TALIBAN, ESPECIALLY OMAR

relationships.detail: The Taliban interlocutor, whose identity is redacted, can speak to top-level Taliban. Identification as Mujahid is inferred.
relationships.quote: HE COULD TELL TOP-LEVEL TALIBAN THIS WAS NOT TRUE

relationships.detail: The UN imposed sanctions on the Taliban over bin Ladin, and the Taliban complain about UN condemnation.
relationships.quote: THE CURRENT UN SANCTIONS WOULD CEASE

relationships.detail: The Taliban interlocutor wanted some UNDCP offices to remain inside Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: SOME OF THE UNDCP OFFICES COULD REMAIN INSIDE AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: UNDCP is a UN body, and the interlocutor asked that its offices remain in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: UNDCP OFFICES

relationships.detail: The Ambassador proposed that the Taliban let MacMakin continue her work inside Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: PERMITTING AMCIT MARY MACMAKIN TO CONTINUE HER WORK INSIDE AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: The interlocutor said he had told Kabul officials not to say anything bad about MacMakin. Identification as Mujahid is inferred.
relationships.quote: NOT TO SAY ANYTHING BAD ABOUT MACMAKIN

relationships.detail: The interlocutor proposed channeling aid through the Afghan Red Crescent.
relationships.quote: ASSISTANCE COULD BE OFFERED TO THE AFGHAN PEOPLE THROUGH THE AFGHAN RED CRESCENT

relationships.detail: Taliban officials are based in Kabul.
relationships.quote: HE HAD ALREADY TOLD OFFICIALS IN KABUL

relationships.detail: Pickering is listed in the cable header (FOR P, i.e. Under Secretary for Political Affairs).
relationships.quote: ALSO FOR P

relationships.detail: Ambassador Milam classified the cable and met the Taliban interlocutor as Ambassador at the US Embassy in Islamabad.
relationships.quote: CLASSIFIED BY AMBASSADOR WILLIAM B. MILAM.

relationships.detail: The Taliban interlocutor charged that Masood routinely breaks his word on peace.
relationships.quote: THE OPPOSITION CLAIMS TO SUPPORT PEACE, BUT MASOOD ROUTINELY BREAKS HIS WORD.

relationships.detail: Masood is treated as the leader of the opposition Northern Alliance.
relationships.quote: THE OPPOSITION CLAIMS TO SUPPORT PEACE, BUT MASOOD ROUTINELY BREAKS HIS WORD.

relationships.detail: The Ambassador noted Under Secretary Pickering had made the same points to the Taliban earlier.
relationships.quote: PREVIOUS U.S. REPRESENTATIVES INCLUDING UNDER SECRETARY PICKERING HAD MADE THE SAME POINTS

relationships.detail: Pickering earlier raised the same points with the Taliban in previous US-Taliban meetings.
relationships.quote: PREVIOUS U.S. REPRESENTATIVES INCLUDING UNDER SECRETARY PICKERING HAD MADE THE SAME POINTS

relationships.detail: Mujahid placed a phone call from New York.
relationships.quote: PHONE CALL FROM MUJAHID IN NEW YORK

relationships.detail: Cable sent from Embassy Islamabad to SECSTATE Washington.
relationships.quote: FM AMEMBASSY ISLAMABAD TO SECSTATE WASHDC IMMEDIATE

relationships.detail: The embassy is in Islamabad.
relationships.quote: FM AMEMBASSY ISLAMABAD

relationships.detail: The Taliban wanted UNDCP to remain in Afghanistan and complained about its announced withdrawal.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN WANTED THE UNDCP TO REMAIN IN AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: Omar issued a decree forbidding poppy cultivation and a new edict on educating girls and boys, which Taliban enforce.
relationships.quote: MULLAH OMAR DOES NOT ISSUE MANY DECREES, SO THE TALIBAN ENFORCE THOSE HE DOES PROCLAIM.

relationships.detail: Iran reportedly now supports sanctions on both sides in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: IRAN NOW SUPPORTS SANCTIONS ON BOTH SIDES

relationships.detail: The interlocutor came overland from Kandahar, the Taliban base, to Quetta.
relationships.quote: CAME OVERLAND FROM KANDAHAR. TO QUETTA, THEN FLEW TO ISLAMABAD

relationships.detail: UN and NGOs distribute American food aid to Afghans under Taliban control.
relationships.quote: IT IS AMERICAN FOOD THAT THE UN AND NGO'S DISTRIBUTE TO AFGHANS.

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin is the man the US says blew up two embassies and remains a sworn enemy of the US.
relationships.quote: A MAN WHO PROCLAIMS HIMSELF THE SWORN ENEMY OF THE UNITED STATES AND ITS PEOPLE

key_claims: The Taliban interlocutor did not challenge US evidence against Bin Ladin or repeat stock Taliban proposals, and promised to work behind the scenes.
He sought assurances that Bin Ladin is the central US concern and that the US is not set on destroying the Taliban.
The Taliban claimed to be trying to control Bin Ladin and said they saved his life.
The embassy was unsure whether the interlocutor spoke for all the Taliban, especially Mullah Omar.
The US told the Taliban that UN sanctions would cease if Bin Ladin were expelled to face justice.
The interlocutor asked for goodwill gestures such as advance notice of aid, a response to the poppy ban, and UNDCP staying in Afghanistan.
The embassy recommended low-cost gestures, such as a statement on the drug ban and donating two cars, but was skeptical of aid via the Red Crescent or directly through the Taliban.
